requirements.text: their premium support contract ... finance wants the amount rebalanced to around 27.315 grand dollars
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM contract WHERE contract_id = 101 AND contract_price = 27315
assumptions: Russell, Johnson and Clark is account 40, which holds two contracts: 101 (support) and 100 (warranty)

'premium support contract' read as the account's only support-type contract, 101; the premium entitlement (344) hangs on the warranty contract 100, but the request names the warranty contract separately
'around 27.315 grand dollars' read as 27315 (27.315 thousand); it is a whole number, so the policy's rounding rule changes nothing

requirements.text: their warranty contract, the price needs to be lifted by about twenty-five percent of whatever value is currently stored
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM contract WHERE contract_id = 100 AND contract_price = 2678
assumptions: contract 100 is account 40's only warranty contract; its stored price is 2142
2142 x 1.25 = 2677.5; the policy rounds contract prices off when decimals are present, giving 2678 (half up and half to even agree)

requirements.text: only if that's the case, go ahead and replace it with their new uk contact line +44-7700-982-441
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user WHERE user_id = 55 AND phone = '+12125516299'
assumptions: the primary contact of account 40 is contact 89, whose portal user is 55 (Bethany Barnes)
user 55's stored phone is +12125516299, a US (+1) number, not an India (+91) one, so the condition fails and the phone must not be replaced

requirements.text: be sure the contact is associated with the correct location Smith Llc Hq - London
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user WHERE user_id = 55 AND location_id = 903
assumptions: the contact table has no location column; the contact's location is its portal user's location_id
Smith Llc Hq - London is location 903, the only location with that name
'be sure' read as unconditional, independent of the phone condition, kept from the benchmark check; the request's wording could also tie it to the phone condition

requirements.text: check their primary contact the team said the profile might still be carrying that old india branch number
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user WHERE user_id IN (681, 726) AND phone IN ('+916769200358', '+916883406886')
assumptions: users 681 and 726 are the portal users of account 40's non-primary contacts (90 and 91) and do carry India (+91) numbers; the request limits the change to the primary contact, so their phones keep their seed values

disagreement: phone: A IN ('+916769200358', '+916883406886'), B LIKE '+91%'; chose A's because both hold on the seed and the exact stored numbers are tighter: a replacement with any other India number would pass the looser form

notes:
disagreement: the phone predicate of the stay on the non-primary contacts' users (exact stored numbers against any India number); chose the exact numbers as the tighter form, logged on that requirement.
The benchmark's user check tests phone and location together; here it is carried by two requirements, one that the phone keeps its US number (the India-number condition is false on the seed) and one that the location becomes 903. The premium entitlement of account 40 (entitlement 344) hangs off the warranty contract 100, so 'premium support contract' could be misread as contract 100; the request names the warranty contract separately, which leaves contract 101 (type support) as the premium support contract. Location 903 is named after another account (Smith LLC), but the request names it explicitly and locations carry no account. The quarterly billing structure has no column in the contract table, so only the price is tested. The request's closing 'realign all of that so everything stays consistent' adds no further change. The new UK line is never written, so its storage format (the seed stores phones without hyphens) does not arise. The acting user (user 32, admin) is inactive in the seed; the policy grants admin responsibilities by default and does not bar an inactive user from acting, so the updates are still expected.
